dataList.dlg: That old friend left me with quite the troublesome little fellow...

Just as he said... You certainly are masterful at making a fine cup of ssanghwa-cha.
... Now, if only you could prove useful in any other capacity.

Life runs more smoothly when people lend one another a hand, does it not? It need not be some grand gesture. When you step out for lunch, bring something back for the colleague buried in work. Cooperation begins with learning to spare someone that much consideration.
Is it nightfall already...? Lately, I've been spending so much time clearing contracts in the gloom that the hour alone is enough to set my nerves on edge.

Don Quixote. Sinclair. If you have the time to waste gawking at that greenhorn, I'm sure you can spare some for your equipment. You know the drill—check that the power comes on, make sure nothing catches when you swing your arms... You both know by now that the smallest inattention can cost lives on the battlefield.

You want to storm the Library this instant and reclaim the books of your colleagues? I don't think so. It's a shame your judgment has yet to catch up to what promise you have in combat.
Take a few deep breaths while the kids finish preparing. And remember this before we depart: as soon as I see your impatience starting to trip us up on the battlefield... you'll be the first one I stab dead.

The Associations, the Wings, the Fingers...  For all their reach, they proved to be clueless about what to make of the Distortions. Even the phenomenon's supposed connection to the Library has nothing behind it but guesswork...
Hmm... The Distortion Detective—I should have questioned that suspicious individual while I had the chance.

... Don't flatter yourself—truly selfless people don't exist. Even self-sacrifice is ultimately a self-serving excuse.
You seem utterly convinced that you're acting for the good of your Office... That foolish conviction will slowly eat away at your peers and lead them to damnation.

That was the first time I had ever seen the Circus in person. Their lair was mysterious and terrifyingly bleak, enough to make my skin crawl.
The performance that followed could have passed for a festival in hell, for lack of a better word—their movements followed no specific pattern, and every prediction fell apart. I was forced to run afresh the numbers of possible outcomes at every turn.
... A welcome quiet spell, you say? Hah. A Fixer Office starved of work is nothing to be pleased about.

Rather generous with your intel, aren't you? An unwise habit when facing a hunter of the City.
There are no more possible scenarios left to calculate—just a swift, sure thrust to stab you through.

Hey, kids. Preparations complete, I trust?
<color=#8b9c15>Of course.</color>
<color=#ffef23>Aye, 'tis all in order!</color>
We can't afford to bother with courtesy when our very lives are at risk.
As discussed, we will communicate by hand signals. Keep your distance and your focus on the enemies.
Engage for collision!
Still wet behind the ears.
Tsk. I used to be sharper.
This is the price of your uncertain actions.
... Perhaps the years... have caught up with me, too...
Stabbed right through the heart of it.
Did thinking it through never occur to you?

They've slipped away already... The 8 o'clock Circus is more trouble than I accounted for.
Couldn't put an end to the case, but we've sized up the job pretty well. Let's settle the outstanding business another day.

It seems I haven't lost my edge after all—not one of them proved to be a proper match in the end. Heh... I may even have the better of that old friend of mine by now.
Kids, wrap things up if you're done securing the books. We're heading back. You can scuffle all you like once we're back in the Office.
... The escape apparatus worked... Hah, can't believe I've gotten this soft... Guess age finally caught up with us... my old friend... and I both.
